title: The Arm
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Two bones, one forearm. Which one is glowing?
This is the right arm, shoulder to wrist.
Which bone is it?
Two bones run along the forearm.
The glowing one is on the thumb side.
It's B. The radius.
Why it matters: a fall on your hand often breaks it near the wrist.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: Hit this bone's elbow end and it's not funny. Name it.
Watch the long bone that's glowing.
Which bone is it?
It runs from your shoulder to your elbow.
The femur is its match, but in your thigh.
It's C. The humerus.
Why it matters: the funny bone tingle is a nerve, not this bone.

title: The Arm
question: What's its everyday name?
lines: This flat, triangle-shaped bone sits on your upper back.
We're looking at the right shoulder from behind.
What's the everyday name of this bone?
The collarbone is a slim bone at the front of the shoulder.
This broad, flat bone glides over your ribs when you move your arm.
It's A. The shoulder blade, or scapula.
Why it matters: it gives your shoulder muscles a wide anchor.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone forms the elbow's point?
lines: Lean on your elbow. This glowing bone is what you feel.
Watch the long forearm bone that's glowing.
Which bone forms the point of the elbow?
The humerus meets the elbow, but it ends above the point.
The point is the olecranon, part of the pinky-side forearm bone.
It's D. The ulna.
Why it matters: your triceps pulls on that point to straighten the arm.

title: The Arm
question: Which bone is glowing?
lines: A slim bone runs from your breastbone to your shoulder.
Look at the glowing bone across the top of the chest.
Which bone is glowing?
The scapula is the broad bone behind the shoulder.
It's C. The clavicle.
Why it matters: it's one of the bones people break most in a fall.

title: The Arm
question: How many bones are in the forearm?
lines: Between your elbow and wrist, how many bones are there?
Watch the glowing bones of the forearm.
How many bones are in the forearm?
The upper arm has just one: the humerus.
It's C. Two: the radius and the ulna.
Why it matters: two bones let you rotate your palm up and down.

title: The Arm
question: Which girdle do these bones form?
lines: Two bones team up to hold your arm to your body.
Look at the two glowing bones at the top of the shoulder.
Which girdle do these bones form?
The pelvic girdle does the same job for your legs.
It's B. Together they form the shoulder girdle.
Why it matters: this girdle lets your arm swing in almost any direction.
